events.intent: Describe current surroundings at game start
events.response:
"Come fly with me from Whitby's cosey harbour to stranger shores.
Come now, as light thickens, and the crow makes wing to rookery wood. Tempests
    rise as great bloody hands, to tear down our safe, homely lives.
Come with me on dragon wings to wicked woods, where night's black agents to
    their preys do rouse."
Dracula - Prince of Darkness
by Paul Johnson. 
www.wolfman.co.uk.
Release 3 / Serial number 051012 / Inform v6.31 Library 6/11 

An open field

 As night approaches, and thick storms rise out from troubled skies.
   Like a spectre you appear.
   Called by a clap of thunder.

A messenger of death, the ghastly owl flutters, and with dreary shrieks he 
passes you by.

From somewhere far away a church bell sounds some early hour. Its sound crawls 
slowly through cold, mist laden air. 
A dead chime.

The bell has called you.
Out of space, out of time...

It is night. You find yourself standing in a grass field, surrounded by dark, 
shadowy trees. To the NORTH, the back stones of some ruined gothic structure 
rises high into the nights sky, silhouetted against a blood red moon.

It's black empty, windows, like eyes watch you far below.

>

events.response:
Abbey ruins
As you walk through the mist towards the ruins you see a sign that reads.

"WHITBY ABBEY."

With a crack of thunder, through darkened air a flash of lightning comes, so 
broad and so bright, the Abbey seems on fire.

From high up, within one of the empty windows, the figure of a woman appears. 
Half hidden in the lions roar of the thunderclap, she calls to you.

"Why came you here?
Unwise...unwise...unwise!"

Lightning flashes, and when you look again she is gone.

All around you are the stone ruins of Whitby Abbey. A noble ruin of immense 
size.

Beautiful once.

Now all that is left are the great, dark walls. Their immense black stones 
eroded away by a century of sea wind.  From high up, two empty windows watch 
your progress far below. To the NORTH, beyond the Abbey's stone wall, you can 
hear the sea crashing against the rocks far below.

SOUTH leads to an open field, while a path leads WEST.

Tell me what to do.
>
events.expected_outcome: Move north to new location

The letter written on fine blue notepaper reads;


Help me!

Over our blessed little harbour a shadow of horror has risen.
A spectre has arrived on a wrecked Russian ship.
I implore you to come, and seek out Abraham Van Helsing M.D. He is here in 
Whitby tonight.
Now, I live under a suffocating cloud of evil, O horrible, O horrible, Most 
horrible!
I must seek out sanctuary, I will go where evil cannot venture, the church.

Love.
Lucy Westenra.



What now?
>

As you step into the graveyard, an immense black hound bounds past you, almost 
pushing you over as it gallops from the Abbey down the stone steps towards the 
town.

The graveyard lies high up over the town, giving it a full view of the harbour 
and the bay, where the headland stretches out into the sea.

The graveyard descends so steeply over the harbour that some of the graves have 
fallen into the sea. A bench is positioned to give a view of the harbour.  To 
the NORTH is a small parish church. To the EAST, a small path leads back up to 
the Abbey. Stone steps lead DOWN to the harbour.

shadows on the floor, under the cover of a black, matted blanket. From the

straw covers the floor. In the orange flickering light, you can just make out

human sweat and fear. Despite the brazier, the room is cold. Rats scurry about 
through the straw. The only entrance is the NORTH door.

This engine of death and destruction stops, and for the first time, those eyes 
look away from you, down to the small golden apple you hold upon one bloody and 
trembling hand. A head, as big as a race horse, lowers to sniff at the apple.

Its savage jaw opens and gently it eats the apple. When it looks back up, you 
see tears from those terrible eyes. Tears flowing down that savage face of 
death. The thing stands on powerful back legs and howls into the night. The 
howl turns into a scream of pain.

The wolf goes berserk. You are knocked sideways as the wolf, in agony, spins 
around in some awful dance of death. The thing lands awkwardly like a fallen 
racehorse. There is an eruption of blood that covers you, and all around you.

as large as a snake, emerges from the beast's ear. It slithers away across the 
ground. The steaming, twitching pile of fur and muscle that was a wolf, now 
looks human and smaller in size.
